title: Medical ward rounds in verbal and non-verbal intensive care patients
summary: In intensive care units, patients are discussed at the bedside every day, and many can barely follow the conversation. In this study, patients wear glasses that record where they are looking. A conversation following the usual routine is compared with one deliberately arranged to be easier to follow, in order to test whether patients can then follow it better.
conditions: Critically ill patients receiving intensive care treatment with limited ability to participate in the medical ward round.

interventions.name: Ward round in its usual structure, unchanged. For each participant, one ward round is recorded from the patient's perspective using eye-tracking glasses.

Ward round in a structurally adapted format, including positioning the speaker within the patient's field of view, addressing the patient directly at defined points, and use of visual aids. Recording as in Arm 1.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Treatment in the intensive care unit and participation in the structured interprofessional ward round; preserved arousal (Richmond Agitation-Sedation Scale −1 to +1); no delirium (Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU-7 = 0); informed consent from the patient or their legal representative.
Exclusion criteria:
No informed consent; sedation or delirium outside the defined thresholds; severe visual impairment precluding gaze recording; clinical or anatomical reasons preventing the eye-tracking glasses from being worn.
